epistemic_policy: Every discovered record remains CANDIDATE_UNREVIEWED until human review.
Similarity does not imply historical descent, common origin or diffusion.
Publication, version-of-record, issue, index and discovery dates are preserved separately where available.
Archaeological observations are separated from inferred symbolic, ritual, social or cognitive meaning.
Ancient-DNA affinity, morphology, culture, language, technology and social identity are not interchangeable variables.
Imputed, predicted or model-classified values are not treated as directly observed measurements.
Historical diagnosis or identity is never inferred from resemblance to modern biomedical categories.

new_candidates.title: Differential bioarchaeological assessment of an intraoral stone object from a Warring States-period Qin burial, China
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: A structured differential assessment of an intraoral stone object finds no evidence supporting sustained antemortem prosthetic use; deliberate postmortem placement remains plausible, but taphonomic entry/displacement cannot be excluded because the original object-sediment-bone relationship was not documented before removal.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Object-with-body association is not sufficient evidence of ritual, intentional placement, dentistry, status or belief. Missing excavation microcontext materially limits interpretation.

new_candidates.title: The initial pathways of broomcorn millet (Panicum miliaceum) into Europe based on AMS dates and stable carbon isotope data
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Integrates 70 direct radiocarbon dates from charred millet grains, including 16 new AMS dates, with Bayesian chronology and stable-carbon-isotope evidence. The authors identify the western Pontic Steppe as the earliest secure European evidence and report subsequent synchronous appearances in the Carpathian Basin, Southeastern Europe and the Caucasus, with later introduction in Anatolia.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Crop movement does not demonstrate population migration, language spread, cultural descent or a single dispersal mechanism. Route and chronology claims remain bounded to the dated archaeobotanical/isotopic record.

new_candidates.title: Words of warning about radiocarbon dating medieval human bones
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Analysis of 27 Danish monastic burials with elevated nitrogen-15 highlights freshwater-fish reservoir effects that can make human-bone radiocarbon ages anomalously old, in some cases apparently predating convent construction.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: This is a dating-risk and correction issue, not a universal invalidation of human-bone radiocarbon dating. Reservoir magnitude is context- and diet-dependent and requires independent assessment.

new_candidates.title: Modelling Local Strontium Isotope Baselines from Human Isotopic Data Using Machine Learning: Implications for Past Mobility Studies
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Introduces MobSr, trained on roughly 3,000 human-enamel samples from 86 sites, with open code and training data. Reported 87-95% performance is agreement with published local/non-local classifications, not validation against independently known residential histories.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: The training labels inherit prior archaeological interpretations and possible circularity. Model probability is not direct evidence of true mobility; assumptions weaken in highly mobile or geologically atypical contexts.

new_candidates.title: Archaic ancestry inference in imputed ancient human genomes
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Evaluates archaic-ancestry inference after genotype imputation of low-coverage ancient genomes and reports improved recovery of introgressed haplotypes; the version of record is dated 2026-09-04.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Imputed genotypes are model-reconstructed values, not directly observed genotypes. Archaic-segment inference does not encode language, culture, identity, belief or artifact authorship. Preserve observed versus imputed provenance at field level.

new_candidates.title: Psychedelic Use Covaries with Psychological Flexibility Through Mystical Experiences: Results of a Retrospective Web Survey
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: A retrospective web survey of more than 200 participants reports an indirect association between psychedelic use and psychological flexibility through self-reported mystical experience measures. The item surfaced in the current PubMed candidate feed.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Retrospective self-report and mediation are not causal evidence. Modern psychedelic use cannot be projected onto ancient ritual, shamanism, religion, or archaeological residues without independent contextual evidence.

new_candidates.title: A Dataset of Wolof Ajami Manuscripts for HTR and OCR
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Releases an open-source dataset of manually segmented and transcribed 20th-century Wolof Ajami handwritten and printed manuscripts in ALTO format, plus transcriptions and tools. Evaluated Arabic-script recognition models show very high character-error rates, highlighting the need to preserve manual transcription provenance.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: OCR/HTR output is not a historical-source transcription unless validated. Manuscript language, script and genre must not be collapsed into religion, ethnicity or private belief. Community provenance and culturally appropriate use should be reviewed even where the technical dataset is openly licensed.

contradictions_and_pressures.summary: An object recovered with or inside human remains cannot be classified as intentional mortuary placement without contextual/taphonomic support; the Qin oral-object case leaves deliberate postmortem placement plausible but not distinguishable from non-intentional movement.

The updated directly dated millet corpus supports the western Pontic Steppe as the earliest secure European evidence, synchronous later appearances across several adjacent regions, and later Anatolian adoption.
Freshwater-fish reservoir effects can make medieval human-bone radiocarbon ages anomalously old. Any NOEMA dates based on human bone in aquatic-diet contexts require reservoir-risk review.

MobSr performance measures concordance with expert-derived locality labels rather than independently known residential histories; automated mobility probabilities must retain training-label provenance and contextual assumptions.

Improved archaic ancestry inference from imputed low-coverage ancient genomes requires explicit observed-versus-imputed field provenance; reconstructed genotypes must not be presented as direct measurements.

A modern retrospective association between psychedelic use, mystical-experience scores and psychological flexibility is hypothesis-generating only and cannot ground historical altered-state or ritual inference.

Wolof Ajami benchmark error rates show that automated recognition of underrepresented historical scripts can be highly unreliable; NOEMA historical-source ingestion should distinguish manual transcription, validated OCR and raw model output.

dating_revisions.summary: Reassess NOEMA crop-transmission chronology against 70 directly dated millet samples and the authors’ revised regional sequence.
